At runtime: wandb.init logs to Weights & Biases (entity/project placeholders in config)

Optional: configs/qd/mutation/svd_uniform_noise.yaml expects a local 'llama3_svd.pt' torch file that is NOT in the tree and has no documented download
entry_points: main.py main (hydra entry: sets up Celery in solo/worker/main mode, wandb.init, then run_qd)

main.py run_qd (the QD loop: evaluates seed models to seed per-task archives, then for num_generation generations dispatches merge_models jobs, cycling the target task every flip_interval, inserts improved children into each task's MAP-Elites-style archive_map, saves archive JSON + elite-map PNG per generation, deletes stale model dirs)

main.py Worker.merge_models (one QD step on a GPU worker: sample two parents from the target-task archive, crossover.merge -> mutator.mutate -> _eval_model on all tasks, compute quality + behaviour-characteristic bin ids, save child with save_pretrained only if it improves some archive cell; optional per-task CMA-ES ask/tell over merge+mutation hyperparameters)
crossover/model_linear.py ModelwiseLinearMerge._merge (task-vector arithmetic: child = base + sum(w_i * (parent_i - base)) / sum(w), w ~ Normal(1+mean, std))

mutation/gaussian_mutator.py GaussianMutator._mutate and mutation/svd_uniform_mutator.py SVDUniformMutator._mutate (add Gaussian noise to every tensor, or add U diag(rand*s) V^T from a precomputed task-vector SVD)
sampler/elite_sampler.py EliteSampler.sample and sampler/random_sampler.py RandomSampler.sample (parent selection from the archive, quality- and bin-weighted or uniform)

tasks/base.py BaseTask.get_q_and_bc / tasks/mbpp.py MBPPTask / tasks/agentbench_os.py AgentBenchOSTask / tasks/agentbench_db.py AgentBenchDBTask (evaluation-only: run fishfarm task on the vLLM model, return quality and BC bin ids)
utils/helpers.py load_hf_params_to_vllm (copies HF state_dict tensors into the live vLLM engine so merged weights can be evaluated without reloading), save_archive_map, plot_elite_map
example_input: configs/config.yaml (hydra): base_model_path meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct; three SakanaAI Llama-3-8B-Instruct expert seed models; tasks agentbench_os, mbpp, agentbench_db; qd.num_generation 1200, flip_interval 1, use_cma False; crossover ModelwiseLinearMerge std 0.01; mutation GaussianMutator rate 0.0003; sampling RandomSampler seed 42
example_output: Hydra output dir with models/gen_<N>/ (safetensors checkpoints of archive-improving children), archives/gen<N>_archive_map.json (per-task dict of BC-bin tuple -> {model_path, quality, sampling_freq}), images/gen<N>_elite_map_train.png, plus wandb logs; README gives no sample output

vLLM 0.3.0 (per requirements) and its private engine internals (llm.llm_engine.driver_worker.model_runner.model)
Docker daemon (MySQL containers for DBBench, Ubuntu containers for OS-Interaction)
RabbitMQ + Redis brokers for multi-worker Celery mode
host_class: Linux + one or more NVIDIA GPUs able to hold Llama-3-8B in bf16 (vLLM), CPython 3.10, Docker, network access to huggingface.co (gated Meta Llama 3 licence acceptance), evalplus dataset hosts and wandb
built_to: Train ('Training' section of README) LLM agents by cyclically applying quality-diversity search over merged Llama-3-8B-Instruct expert models across three agent skills (OS interaction, coding/MBPP, database/DBBench) -- the README itself only gives install and run steps under the title 'Agent Skill Acquisition for Large Language Models via CycleQD (ICLR 2025)'.
pressure: NOT_FOUND_AT_PIN (README contains no motivation or abstract text; only title, links, install and run instructions, and bibtex)
success_means: NOT_FOUND_AT_PIN in README; from the code, success is the quality metric per task (mbpp_base_pass@1 from evalplus; AgentBench OS-Interaction and DBBench success rates) of elites stored in each task's archive, plotted as elite maps and logged to wandb
main_loop_one_sentence: run_qd seeds one MAP-Elites-style archive per task by evaluating the expert seed models, then for each generation picks the next task in a fixed cycle (flip_interval), has a worker sample two parents from that task's archive, merge them as weighted task vectors on the shared base model (ModelwiseLinearMerge), add Gaussian (or SVD-structured) noise, evaluate the child on all tasks via vLLM, and insert the child into every task archive cell (indexed by the other tasks' scores binned as behaviour characteristics) where its quality beats the incumbent, optionally letting a per-task CMA-ES adapt the merge/mutation hyperparameters from the child's fitness.
behavioral_entry_point: main.py:Worker.merge_models (order of sample/merge/mutate/eval, archive insertion rule, CMA-ES fitness); crossover/model_linear.py:ModelwiseLinearMerge._merge; mutation/gaussian_mutator.py:GaussianMutator._mutate; sampler/elite_sampler.py:EliteSampler.sample; main.py:run_qd (task cycling via cfg.qd.flip_interval); all swappable via hydra configs/qd/*
